title: Colombia's 'El Tigre' takes fight to cartels as Trump alliance takes shape
summary: Abelardo de la Espriella claims over 32,000 arrests in 10 weeks as Colombia joins Trump's anti-cartel coalition, pivoting away from predecessor's policies.
story: Known by his nickname 'El Tigre,' the president has intensified his offensive against armed groups. (COLOMBIAN GOVERNMENT TV via Reuters.)

President Abelardo de la Espriella means business when it comes to his war against the cartels. Colombia's new president, known by the nickname of "El Tigre." was voted in on a law-and-order ticket and so far his actions in fighting the cartels are seemingly paying dividends — not just in Colombia but in Washington, too.

Recently, he arrived at the Barranquilla police command around the early hours of the morning as 587 police officers and soldiers raided 50 locations across the Caribbean port city and its suburbs in Operation Blindaje 360. A few days earlier, domestic Colombian news outlets had widely publicized a recording intercepted by Colombian police of "Keko," the alleged leader of a gang called "Los del Freseo," boasting that de la Espirella had nothing on him.
"The Tiger's got nothing. Let him come out, and we'll put lead in him," Keko allegedly said on the recording.
Then, before dawn, Colombia's president had tracked him down and was face to face with him, all caught on tape.

According to a video released by his presidential office, El Tigre told Keko the gang leader was "a tough guy on the phone… but the look of the fear on his face matched that of his many victims." The sweep ended with 72 arrests.
ANTI-CARTEL HARDLINER CHANNELS TRUMP IN BID TO END COLOMBIA'S LEFTIST ERA IN PIVOTAL ELECTION

President Abelardo de la Espriella speaks at the Jose Maria Cordova Military School in Bogota on Aug. 26, 2026, after Colombia's government announced plans to classify guerrilla fighters, drug traffickers and other criminal groups as "terrorists." (Raul Arboleda/AFP via Getty Images)

The theatrics played to a large audience who had long argued that former leftist President Gustavo Petros’s policy of pursuing engagement with drug traffickers had left Colombia more vulnerable to organized crime. Colombian and Venezuelan cartels were reportedly dominating the space left by the power vacuum which emerged from the lack of effective law enforcement.

His government is also seeking to reverse Petro’s "total peace" policy, which pursued negotiations with several armed organizations. Before taking office, de la Espriella announced that he would dismantle key elements of the policy and reactivate arrest warrants against members of illegal armed groups.

Nearly three months into his term, the 48-year-old lawyer has scrapped his predecessor's "total peace" talks, ordered every armed group treated as a terrorist organization and claimed more than 32,000 arrests. He is doing it arm in arm with Washington.
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella shows up after a raid in Barranquilla to confront Keko face-to-face on Oct. 16 2026. (Abelardo De La Espriella @Abelaespriella)

A dual U.S.-Colombian citizen who lived in Miami before running for president, he has brought Colombia into President Donald Trump's anti-cartel coalition. Last month, he personally handed a guerrilla boss accused of supplying Mexico's Sinaloa Cartel to DEA agents with his hands and feet shackled.
The prisoner, Geovany Andrés Rojas, alias "Araña," is alleged to have led the "Comandos de la Frontera" dissidents and now faces narco-terrorism charges in Southern California.

"The option of dialogue is completely exhausted," de la Espriella told troops after his Aug. 7 inauguration. In an Oct. 12 address, he put the tally at 32,503 arrests, 33 ringleaders taken out of action and 679 drug-production sites destroyed or disabled. He has signed more than 100 extradition orders, including five for former armed-group peace negotiators wanted in the U.S. whose handovers the previous government had frozen.
‘DONROE’ DOCTRINE AND CONSERVATIVE VICTORIES SQUEEZE CARTELS IN LATIN AMERICA

An Army operation in La Gabarra, Tibú, results in the detention of five FARC dissidents and the seizure of weapons and communications equipment on Oct. 6, 2026. (Abelardo De La Espriella @Abelaespriella)

The offensive reaches deep into the countryside, where conflict monitor ACLED counted August as the deadliest month for clashes between security forces and armed groups since it began tracking Colombia in 2018.

In late August he warned FARC dissident chief Iván Mordisco: "When you least expect it, a bomb is going to fall on you." Two days later, he walked among the bagged bodies of 23 suspected dissidents at an army base in Guaviare, and troops killed the top commander of a paramilitary-rooted trafficking group in La Guajira.

Colombia became the 19th member of Trump's Shield of the Americas coalition in August, and War Secretary Pete Hegseth said Bogotá had authorized "joint military operations to destroy terrorists and terror networks domestically." The administration has pledged $1 billion in security aid, pending congressional approval, and Marine Gen. Francis Donovan, head of U.S. Southern Command, has toured Colombian bases.

However, speaking on-camera to Fox News Digital, Colombian Vice President José Manuel Restrepo said while his country is embracing Trump’s push for a new security alliance across the Western Hemisphere, he drew a clear line on the role American forces would play inside Colombia, saying Colombian troops — not U.S. forces — will carry out operations against the country’s armed groups.
PENTAGON SENDS HUNDREDS OF ARMY TROOPS TO LATIN AMERICA FOR TRAINING AS DRUG-TRAFFICKING CAMPAIGN EXPANDS
President Donald Trump and War Secretary Pete Hegseth during the "Shield of the Americas" Summit at Trump National Doral in Miami, Florida, March 7, 2026. (Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images)

According to Benjamin Gedan, a senior fellow and director of the Latin America Program at the Stimson Center in Washington who previously served as a South America director in the White House, the last few years were an outlier:

"For decades, the United States and Colombia closely cooperated to fight guerrillas and organized crime. Plan Colombia was celebrated by both Republicans and Democrats. The Colombian military is well-trained and battle-tested. Renewed close cooperation between Bogotá and Washington is a cornerstone of the renewed U.S. focus on security in Latin America," he said.

"Still, flashy military strikes on criminal targets will not answer the mail. These groups are well-armed, well-funded and thrive in regions with little state presence. Images of criminals in body bags may give the impression of forward progress after the failed strategy of Colombia’s last leader, much as videos of exploding speedboats have become the calling card of the Shield of the Americas. In both cases, a more sophisticated strategy is needed to deal lasting blows to criminal groups," Gedan argued.
CRIME, KIDNAPPINGS AND DRONE ATTACKS FLAGGED IN US WARNING FOR BORDER REGION
Americans are urged not to travel within five miles of the Colombia-Venezuela border due to crime, kidnapping and armed conflict. (Schneyder Mendoza/AFP via Getty Images)

Oscar Palma, a professor of security studies at the University of Rosario in Bogotá, said it is still a little too early to assess the change in policies and affirm they will be fruitful within the Colombian context. "Beyond the policing acts themselves, there is the subjective feeling of security with debates within Colombian society on whether this open war strategy brings more or less security to the population. Many argue that the gangs are acting now more forcefully to defend their territories and business deals, while others believe that a strong police presence will eventually lead to less organized crime."

Palma said there is a false dichotomy between having to choose all-out war or dialogue in order to achieve peace with groups such as the FARC and other gang leaders: "It is a fiction that you will come to zero combatants simply pursuing one strategy or the other—all-out war will never zero down those combating in the FARC and organized crime just as peace talks, especially if carried out in a misguided policy such as the one led by [Gustavo] Petros, will achieve real results."

He said, "A better example is the strategy carried out by President [Juán Manuel] Santos during the dealings with the FARC, which led to a much safer Colombia: there were talks, but those were part of a bigger strategy of also fighting these groups with arms and bringing them to justice," he added.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"There is a wave of freedom, a wave of democracy, a wave of free market… There is a new momentum for the region and we have to take advantage of that momentum. That's what I said to President Trump," Restrepo told Fox News Digital. "If we want to keep and preserve democracy in the region, the Shield of the Americas is going to be the best opportunity to do it."

Solly Boussidan is an international journalist covering Latin America for Fox News Digital. He has previously covered international affairs, war, finance and travel for several U.S. and international outlets. He is currently based in Brazil.

title: Six people killed, at least a dozen injured in shooting at main market square of Krakow, Poland
summary: Authorities in Poland are investigating a shooting that left six people dead and at least a 15 injured in the Main Market Square in Krakow, a cultural center of the historic city, according to officials.
story: Authorities in Poland are investigating a shooting on Saturday that left six people dead and at least a 15 injured in the Main Market Square in Krakow, a cultural center of the historic city, according to officials.
Four women and two men were killed in the mid-day ambush in the city’s popular commerce and tourist destination, police said.
A police officer was seriously wounded in the shooting and is undergoing surgery. He was shot at three times, according to a statement from Minister of the Interior Affairs Marcin Kierwiński.

The attacker, a Polish national, was shot by police at the scene and taken to the hospital around 3 p.m. local time. The shots were fired from a vehicle moving through the area, Krakow officials said in a series of posts X.

An earlier post from the city’s official municipal government account said that investigators were working to determine the scale of the incident. The city announced a mourning period in recognition of the tragedy through Nov. 11.

Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Krakow police, told TVN24 that the perpetrator was wearing military-style fatigues and he used a military-type long gun in the attack. Police found many pieces of other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car.

Kierwiński said authorities are evaluating reports that the gunman was fixated on far-right political ideologies. The shooter, who the official did not identify, is in serious condition and is undergoing surgery.
For Subscribers

Dramatic video posted on social media shows what appears to be an injured police officer firing at the suspect before dropping to his knees and rolling over onto his back. The officer, who did not appear to have backup nearby, is seen struggling to reload his firearm and appeared to be clutching his right arm.

It was unclear if the officer seen in the video is the same one cited in the interior affairs minister’s update. Małopolska Police wrote in an X post that no officer had been killed, citing what they said were incorrect reports.
Other chilling video clips taken from the scene show a black sedan racing through the square. Dozens of people began running in various directions at the sound of gunfire.
For Subscribers
Some social media clips depict responders attempting life-saving measures on victims. Lifeless bodies could be seen scattered around the streets after the attack.

Taylor Dorfmeister was in the square with his roommate when gunfire erupted. Dorfmeister said there was a delay before the crowd reacted and then everyone began to flee the area. He said he took shelter in a building.
“We ran up the stairs in the building to hide and it was a dead end, which is when I was the most terrified since the gunshots were [loud] and near,” Dorfmeister told NBC News.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk also wrote on social media that police were trying to determine the circumstances surrounding the attack.

“We are just learning details of the horrific mass shooting in Krakow, a savage and murderous attack that’s shattered the peace of Poland,” Tom Rose, the U.S. ambassador to Poland, wrote on X. “America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Krakow.”

The Main Market Square sits at the heart of Krakow’s medieval Old Town, where centuries of trade transpired under changing political and religious influences. Laid out in 1257, the sprawling plaza is home to the historic Cloth Hall and St. Mary’s Basilica.
It is considered the largest market square in Europe with history preserved in historical homes, houses of worship and ornate palaces, according to the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.
Mansions throughout the square were home to Polish royalty and aristocrats. It was renamed for Adolf Hitler and served as a Nazi propaganda base during the World War II occupation of Poland.

title: The ‘slam dunk’ that wasn’t: Promising cholesterol drug fails to prevent heart attacks or stroke
summary: An experimental drug that held great promise in driving down a dangerous form of cholesterol didn’t show any measurable impact on heart attack or stroke in a clinical trial.
story: An experimental drug that held great promise in driving down a dangerous form of cholesterol didn’t show any measurable impact on heart attack or stroke in a clinical trial. The failure of the Novartis drug pelacarsen to help people who have high levels of lipoprotein(a) stunned researchers, who called it a massive blow to preventive cardiology.

Results of the clinical trial of pelacarsen, an injection, presented Saturday at a meeting of the American Heart Association, found there were zero decreases in stroke, heart attack, cardiovascular deaths or the number of procedures to open blocked arteries or restore blood flow to the heart.

“I really thought that this was going to be a slam dunk,” said Dr. Amanda Doran, an assistant professor of medicine in the division of cardiovascular medicine at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Vanderbilt was one of nearly 800 sites involved in the clinical trial, called Horizon. “We were pretty invested, so it obviously hurts.”

Pelacarsen targets a stealthy and particularly lethal form of cholesterol called lipoprotein(a), or Lp(a). Much like low-density lipoprotein — LDL, or the “bad” cholesterol — Lp(a) causes plaque to build up in arteries. But it also helps form blood clots, and unlike LDL, it is entirely genetic.
About 1 in 5 Americans have high Lp(a), according to the American Heart Association. Most don’t realize they’re at risk.
Because people are born with those high levels, diet and exercise have no effect. That’s why heart experts have been so keen to find a drug that would handle the problem.
The Horizon trial included 8,322 people with high Lp(a) levels and who’d already had a heart attack, stroke or other heart problem within 10 years of starting the trial.
The drug did reduce Lp(a) significantly, by 78%, compared to a placebo drug that cut levels by 13%.
But that huge reduction ultimately meant nothing in terms of cardiovascular health.
Dr. Steven Nissen, the chief academic officer of the Heart, Vascular & Thoracic Institute at the Cleveland Clinic, led the trial. He said the dismal results took him by “extreme surprise.”

“Everybody, me included, believed that lowering levels of lipoprotein(a) substantially would reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events,” he said. “There is simply no evidence here that people that got more reduction did better.”

The findings, also published Saturday in the New England Journal of Medicine, confounded Nissen and other cardiologists who’ve long known that controlling other markers of heart health — LDL and blood pressure, for example — provides clear benefits.

“I have not seen a more shockingly neutral trial in a while,” said Dr. Karol Watson, co-director of the UCLA Program in Preventive Cardiology and a professor at UCLA’s David Geffen School of Medicine. Watson was not involved with the research.

There are several theories as to why the drug didn’t work as anticipated. It’s possible, Watson said, that the therapy was given too late in life to make a difference. The average age of Horizon’s study participants was 60, and they were followed for an average of five years.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“Remember that Lp(a) is a genetic disorder, so from the time a baby’s conceived, their Lp(a) is high. If we just swooped in in the last five years, maybe that’s too late,” Watson said.

Study participants were also treated aggressively in other ways to drive down their LDL cholesterol and get blood pressure readings into a healthy range. Participants may have also been taking aspirin because of a history of heart attack or stroke, which could have lessened Lp(a)’s clotting risk.
“How much of the Lp(a)-associated risk was remaining? We just don’t know,” Watson said.
Does Lp(a) still matter as a marker of heart health?

Doctors have only recently begun screening for it. Earlier this year, the American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association released guidelines that every adult should have their Lp(a) levels measured. It’s a blood test that’s done once because levels are fixed and don’t change over time.
Experts stress that Lp(a) remains an important and valuable indicator of heart disease risk, even though the Horizon study failed to show any health benefit to driving down Lp(a) levels.

“None of that invalidates Lp(a) as a robust marker of cardiovascular disease risk,” said Dr. John Wilkins, a cardiologist at Northwestern Medicine and a professor in the division of cardiology at Northwestern University’s Feinberg School of Medicine. Wilkins was also one of the authors of the Lp(a) guidelines.

“It’s still worth testing for Lp(a) because it can help identify individuals with a higher probability of an event, and we do have other interventions that can help reduce their risk,” Wilkins said. “It’s just that at present, at least with this particular drug in this particular group of patients, we did not see benefit. That doesn’t mean that we might not find something or some way to lower Lp(a) that reduces risk. We just need more science to figure that out.”

UCLA’s Watson and Vanderbilt’s Doran agreed. “We have really good data to show that Lp(a) levels are predictive of disease,” Doran said. “People who have high Lp(a) need to be aware of that in order to pursue aggressive prevention strategies.”
What’s next in treating Lp(a)?
No further study of pelacarsen is planned, Nissen said, but similar drugs are in the pipeline: Eli Lilly’s lepodisiran, Amgen’s olpasiran and Silence Therapeutics’ zerlasiran.

All are injections that work by blocking the liver’s ability to produce Lp(a), but use different approaches. Pelacarsen is what’s known as an antisense oligonucleotide. The others use a technology called small interfering RNA, or siRNA, and may have fewer side effects, such as injection site reactions, Nissen said, than pelacarsen.
Like pelacarsen, all reduce Lp(a). Clinical trials to show whether they have any real-world heart health effects are ongoing.
Eli Lilly is also studying an oral drug called muvalaplin, and CRISPR gene-editing technology designed to permanently switch off the gene that produces Lp(a) is in early development.
“I’m still so hopeful,” Doran said. “We’re going to get it in the end.”

title: We want to hear your experience with changes to student loan repayment plans
summary: If you’re a student borrower who was required to transition to another plan this year, share your story.
story: President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” has transformed the sprawling federal student loan system — and student borrowers are feeling the effects of the most consequential changes.
For Subscribers

This year, the approximately 7.5 million student borrowers under the Biden-era Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, plan had to select a new one. So far, about 2 million borrowers have done so, after the Education Department warned that the SAVE plan was “illegal” and would be discontinued. The remaining borrowers who did not select a new plan were set to start receiving notices this month informing them that they missed a final deadline and were automatically moved to a new plan.
For Subscribers

The Trump administration has said ending the SAVE plan would help streamline repayment programs while ensuring borrowers are paying off what they owe to the federal government. But student advocacy groups fear lower-income borrowers who had benefited from smaller monthly payments — or even qualified to make no payments at all based on their income — will end up with significantly higher bills under the other available plans.
We want to hear from you, whether you’re in this situation or are facing another challenge related to the recent student loan changes. Please share your experience by filling out the form below.

title: South Carolina man arrested after leaving sleeping 6-year-old daughter in line for Pokémon card release, police say
summary: A man was arrested in Charleston, South Carolina, on Friday after leaving his 6-year-old daughter asleep outside a Target to hold his place in line for the release of a new Pokémon trading card set, police said.
story: A man was arrested in Charleston, South Carolina, on Friday after leaving his 6-year-old daughter asleep outside a Target to hold his place in line for the release of a new Pokémon trading card set, police said.

Officers responded around 2:30 a.m. to the Target in Charleston’s West Ashley neighborhood after a report of an unattended child, the Charleston Police Department said in a news release. They found the girl alone. Police identified the father as John-Michael Dooley, 35, of Johns Island, South Carolina.

Numerous customers had gathered outside the store overnight in anticipation of the release, according to the police. The latest expansion for the bestselling Pokémon Trading Card Game, “Mega Evolution — Delta Reign,” went on sale Friday. The decades-old Japanese franchise, which began as a children’s video game, centers on fictional creatures that players collect, train and battle. Packs starts at around $5.
For Subscribers
The release does not say whether Dooley intended to buy the cards for himself or his daughter.

Witnesses told police that Dooley gave the girl a pillow and blanket before leaving her asleep in line sometime after 1 a.m. After about an hour passed without his return, concerned customers called police, authorities said.
For Subscribers

When Dooley came back to the store, witnesses identified him and he was arrested, according to the release. Police said he admitted that he had gone home and left his daughter unattended so he could keep his place in line.
The child was unharmed and placed in emergency protective custody with the South Carolina Department of Social Services, police said.
Dooley was charged with unlawful conduct toward a child. He is being held at the Al Cannon Detention Center, according to the release, and could not immediately be reached for comment.

Because people are born with those high levels, diet and exercise have no effect. That’s why heart experts have been so keen to find a drug that would handle the problem.
The Horizon trial included 8,322 people with high Lp(a) levels and who’d already had a heart attack, stroke or other heart problem within 10 years of starting the trial.
The drug did reduce Lp(a) significantly, by 78%, compared to a placebo drug that cut levels by 13%.
But that huge reduction ultimately meant nothing in terms of cardiovascular health.
Dr. Steven Nissen, the chief academic officer of the Heart, Vascular & Thoracic Institute at the Cleveland Clinic, led the trial. He said the dismal results took him by “extreme surprise.”

“Everybody, me included, believed that lowering levels of lipoprotein(a) substantially would reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events,” he said. “There is simply no evidence here that people that got more reduction did better.”

The findings, also published Saturday in the New England Journal of Medicine, confounded Nissen and other cardiologists who’ve long known that controlling other markers of heart health — LDL and blood pressure, for example — provides clear benefits.

“I have not seen a more shockingly neutral trial in a while,” said Dr. Karol Watson, co-director of the UCLA Program in Preventive Cardiology and a professor at UCLA’s David Geffen School of Medicine. Watson was not involved with the research.

There are several theories as to why the drug didn’t work as anticipated. It’s possible, Watson said, that the therapy was given too late in life to make a difference. The average age of Horizon’s study participants was 60, and they were followed for an average of five years.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“Remember that Lp(a) is a genetic disorder, so from the time a baby’s conceived, their Lp(a) is high. If we just swooped in in the last five years, maybe that’s too late,” Watson said.

Study participants were also treated aggressively in other ways to drive down their LDL cholesterol and get blood pressure readings into a healthy range. Participants may have also been taking aspirin because of a history of heart attack or stroke, which could have lessened Lp(a)’s clotting risk.
“How much of the Lp(a)-associated risk was remaining? We just don’t know,” Watson said.
Does Lp(a) still matter as a marker of heart health?

Doctors have only recently begun screening for it. Earlier this year, the American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association released guidelines that every adult should have their Lp(a) levels measured. It’s a blood test that’s done once because levels are fixed and don’t change over time.
Experts stress that Lp(a) remains an important and valuable indicator of heart disease risk, even though the Horizon study failed to show any health benefit to driving down Lp(a) levels.

“None of that invalidates Lp(a) as a robust marker of cardiovascular disease risk,” said Dr. John Wilkins, a cardiologist at Northwestern Medicine and a professor in the division of cardiology at Northwestern University’s Feinberg School of Medicine. Wilkins was also one of the authors of the Lp(a) guidelines.

“It’s still worth testing for Lp(a) because it can help identify individuals with a higher probability of an event, and we do have other interventions that can help reduce their risk,” Wilkins said. “It’s just that at present, at least with this particular drug in this particular group of patients, we did not see benefit. That doesn’t mean that we might not find something or some way to lower Lp(a) that reduces risk. We just need more science to figure that out.”

UCLA’s Watson and Vanderbilt’s Doran agreed. “We have really good data to show that Lp(a) levels are predictive of disease,” Doran said. “People who have high Lp(a) need to be aware of that in order to pursue aggressive prevention strategies.”
What’s next in treating Lp(a)?
No further study of pelacarsen is planned, Nissen said, but similar drugs are in the pipeline: Eli Lilly’s lepodisiran, Amgen’s olpasiran and Silence Therapeutics’ zerlasiran.

All are injections that work by blocking the liver’s ability to produce Lp(a), but use different approaches. Pelacarsen is what’s known as an antisense oligonucleotide. The others use a technology called small interfering RNA, or siRNA, and may have fewer side effects, such as injection site reactions, Nissen said, than pelacarsen.
Like pelacarsen, all reduce Lp(a). Clinical trials to show whether they have any real-world heart health effects are ongoing.
Eli Lilly is also studying an oral drug called muvalaplin, and CRISPR gene-editing technology designed to permanently switch off the gene that produces Lp(a) is in early development.
“I’m still so hopeful,” Doran said. “We’re going to get it in the end.”

title: We tried HigherDose’s most popular wellness devices — here’s what’s worth buying
summary: NBC Selected editors spent weeks testing HigherDose’s 6 most popular red light, infrared and PEMF devices to see which ones are actually worth the price.
story: Wellness technology has moved from dermatologists’ offices, spas and physical therapy clinics into our bathrooms and living rooms. LED face masks, infrared sauna blankets, microcurrent devices and PEMF mats now promise to bring treatments once associated with professionals into your home, often for hundreds or even thousands of dollars.

HigherDose is one of the buzziest brands in the category. It launched with its viral infrared sauna blanket and has since expanded into red light face masks, PEMF mats, a red light showerhead filter and more.

But at HigherDose prices, the bigger question is whether these devices are actually worth buying. Six NBC Selected editors spent weeks and, in some cases, months testing six of the brand’s products. Below, we break down what we liked, what we didn’t and who we think each device is best for.
HigherDose is offering an exclusive discount to NBC Selected readers: Use code SELECTED15 for 15% off at HigherDose’s website through December 31, 2026.

Our honest review of HigherDose

The list below includes HigherDose products that NBC Selected staffers have personally tested for months. Our testers generally found them easy to incorporate into their routines and liked their design, comfort and convenience. However, results varied by device, and several require consistent use before you may notice changes. They’re also expensive: Many cost several hundred dollars, making them more of an investment than an impulse buy. HigherDose links to research and provides information about the technologies used in its products on its website. Keep in mind that evidence varies considerably by technology and intended benefit, which we discuss below.

Two of the devices on our list are also FDA-cleared: the Red Light Face Mask and the Red Light Hat. (FDA clearance is not the same as FDA approval; clearance generally means the FDA determined that a device is substantially equivalent to an existing legally-marketed device.)

The Infrared Sauna Blanket was the very first product that HigherDose released, and of the devices we tested for this guide, it has the broadest appeal: It’s simple to use, effects are quickly noticeable and it’s easy to fit in your day-to-day routine.

According to experts in our red light therapy guide, infrared light therapy has been used to treat joint pain for years. Laid flat, the blanket looks like an oversized black sleeping bag made of vegan leather. It plugs into the wall and connects to a small handheld controller with a dial that lets you adjust the heat across eight levels, so you can start low and work your way up as you get used to it. The brand recommends preheating it for about 10 minutes, then zipping yourself in for a 30- to 45-minute session. When you’re done, you let it cool, wipe it down, fold it up and tuck it under a bed or in a closet, which makes it much easier to store away than a full-size sauna.

The purpose of the sauna blanket is to soothe aches and pains and wind down. NBC Selected editorial operations associate Jem Alabi says this product “changed [her] life,” and she regularly falls asleep when using it because she’s so relaxed. “Since I’ve been using it, I’ve been able to [reduce] the soreness I experience after a long work day and commute. I hop in the shower right after and head straight to bed,” she says.

It’s also designed for post-workout recovery: Lauren Swanson, NBC Selected editorial director, used the sauna blanket while training for the New York City marathon two years ago. Though she didn’t notice a measurable difference in her performance, she liked using it as a way to unwind after training. “While I don’t have hard proof that it helped my pace, I did enjoy those 15 minutes of lying down and sweating after a long run,” she says.

Like the sauna blanket, the mat uses infrared heat, but because you lie on top of it rather than zip yourself inside, the experience is less intense and sweaty. Along with infrared, it has pulsed electromagnetic field (PEMF) therapy, which sends low-level electromagnetic waves through your body and has been studied for pain and recovery. However, evidence for many of the broader wellness benefits associated with PEMF products is still limited.

“I’ve been using this mat a few times a week at night to help relax me before bed,” says Alabi, who notes it’s particularly good for times you want to avoid getting sweaty or only have a limited amount of time to use it. “Unlike the sauna blanket, this one doesn’t make you sweaty or require time to heat up, so you can just lie down for as long as you like.”

However, since the mat has 20 pounds of amethyst and obsidian crystals built in, lying down directly on it may feel uncomfortable, so Alabi puts a thin blanket down. You can also buy a cover for the mat directly from HigherDose.

The mat is also fairly large and heavy (it’s around 6 feet long and weighs 43 pounds), which can be cumbersome to roll up and put away. If you’re short on space, HigherDose’s smaller Go Mat has the same technology, but is about half the size and much lighter.

The HigherDose Red Light Face Mask brings the brand’s signature light therapy to a smaller, more targeted format. Red light can have anti-inflammatory properties that can help soothe skin when used consistently, though research is limited, experts previously told us. However, our testers noticed some positive effects on their skin: “I’ve had this mask for about three years and my skin has really improved,” says Alabi. “It reduces the appearance of my pimples overnight and keeps my complexion smooth. I have also experienced hair growth around my hairline, since some of the red light reaches my baby hairs and edges.”

The flexible silicone mask straps over your face, using red and near-infrared light (the biggest difference between the two is how deeply they can penetrate skin) to even out skin tone and reduce inflammation without any heat or mess involved, according to the brand. There is also a neck attachment you can purchase separately to extend those benefits to your neck and chest area. The convenience really sets this face mask apart from other red light masks: You can easily wear the mask while scrolling on your phone or watching TV, and sessions typically run just 10 to 20 minutes.

To use the mask, you want to make sure you have clean skin because products like SPF and heavy moisturizers can block the light, according to HigherDose. The actual mask is made of medical-grade, flexible silicone that contours to the face and a head strap keeps it secure. You can choose a 10- or 20-minute session (HigherDose suggests using it for 10 or 20 minutes three to five times a week). When it runs out of juice, you can recharge it with the included USB-C cable.

This wand, which HigherDose launched in October, is the brand’s latest product in its wellness tech lineup. It’s a lightweight, handheld device that packs three technologies into one: The wand combines an 808-nanometer cold laser, red, near-infrared and blue LED light, and a cooling attachment. These different settings can target concerns like fine lines, acne, redness and puffiness, according to HigherDose.

After using the wand consistently for six weeks, I’ve noticed that my skin feels smoother and looks less red and irritated throughout the day. I also like that it comes with a travel case, a charging cable and mini sizes of the brand’s Light-Activated Peptide Serum and Hydrating Botanical Facial Mist, which you apply first to prep your skin.

There are two light modes: Tone + Tighten and Clear + Calm. The Tone + Tighten mode pairs the laser with 630-nanometer red and 830-nanometer near-infrared light to support collagen and soften the look of fine lines, according to the brand. When I use this setting, I focus it on my forehead, smile lines and jawline. The Clear + Calm setting uses 415-nanometer blue light, which targets acne-causing bacteria and reduces the appearance of redness and breakouts, according to HigherDose. The wand beeps every minute to tell you when to move to a new area, and a full session takes about 10 to 15 minutes.

My favorite part, though, is the cooling attachment. The cryohead cools to either 50 or 54.5 degrees Fahrenheit (you can choose), and when I glide it along my cheekbones, jawline and under my eyes, it feels incredibly refreshing. It helps depuff my face, especially in the morning, and I can even use it over makeup for a quick midday reset.

This shower filter combines two wellness upgrades into one fixture: a filtered showerhead and a red light attachment that bathes your hair, face, and body in light therapy while you rinse. Because it’s built into a step already in your routine, it solves one of the biggest hurdles with red light therapy — actually committing to doing it regularly.

“After two months of testing, I didn’t notice any dramatic changes in my skin or hair that I could confidently attribute to the red light. But the biggest benefit for me was the convenience: Since I shower every day anyway, I didn’t have to remember to set aside separate time for red light therapy,” says NBC Selected commerce editor Mili Godio. She also likes the added control the remote offers: “I easily choose how long each session is, and, depending on what I selected, the light automatically turns off after five, 10 or 15 minutes.” It also took Godio less than 10 minutes to set up.

The HigherDose Red Light Hat takes the brand’s light therapy tech and puts it in one of its most wearable forms. Styled like a baseball hat, the device is lined with red and near-infrared LEDs designed to stimulate the scalp, making it a popular option for people who want to use red light therapy for hair growth without sitting under a stationary panel or dealing with wires. In our guide to red light therapy for hair loss, experts told me that red light can help soothe inflammation on the scalp and promote hair growth in some people with pattern hair loss, though results depend on the type of hair loss and how consistently you use it.

Because it’s cordless and rechargeable, it’s easy to wear around the house while doing chores, reading or working from home, which makes it one of the more realistic red light devices to actually stick with. “I’ve been using this for a few months to see if it would help with my androgenetic alopecia,” says NBC Selected contributor Marilyn La Jeunesse. “The hat itself is very simple to use, you just attach a battery to the back of the device and sit with the hat on dry, clean hair for about ten minutes. After a few weeks of use I’ve noticed more baby hairs on the top of my head.” However, because La Jeunesse used the hat alongside scalp massages and the Cecred Restoring Hair and Edge Drops, she can’t attribute the new growth to the HigherDose hat alone.
What to know before buying HigherDose
While NBC Selected editors have all liked the HigherDose products they’ve tried, there are a few things to be aware of:

The evidence doesn’t support every wellness claim equally. Red light therapy has stronger evidence for certain skin concerns and hair loss. Dermatologists previously told us that red light therapy can help improve fine lines and wrinkles, though the effects are modest compared to more aggressive treatments like laser peels, and a 2025 systematic review found it can work for pattern hair loss. Experts say that evidence around red light and recovery and sleep is more limited. As for PEMF, it has been studied for conditions like osteoarthritis pain, but there’s less evidence supporting some of the broader wellness claims made around consumer devices (like better sleep and less inflammation). Even HigherDose’s less expensive devices sit at a price point that puts them out of reach for many casual wellness dabblers, with a handful of items approaching or exceeding $1,000. You also need to use these products consistently: HigherDose recommends using them multiple times per week for weeks or months to actually see results. How we tested HigherDose products

NBC Selected editors tested HigherDose products at home for at least a month, though most were tested for a minimum of three months. We worked them into our existing routines to see how they hold up with everyday use. We followed the brand’s instructions for each product and judged them on these factors:

Who is HigherDose for?

HigherDose makes the most sense for someone who already knows they enjoy spa-like wellness treatments like red light therapy or infrared heat and wants a convenient way to do them at home. The devices we tested stood out for how easy they were to work into our routines, but less so for dramatic, overnight results. The face mask is hands-free, the hat is cordless, the showerhead is simple to install and the sauna blanket is the perfect alternative to booking a sauna session.

However, these devices only pay off with regular use (usually for weeks or months) and come at a steep price, making them a harder sell if you’re new to red light or infrared therapy, or tend to abandon wellness gadgets after a few uses.

If you do want to splurge, we recommend narrowing down your purchase based on the benefit rather than buying into the HigherDose ecosystem as a whole. We think the sauna blanket is a great entry point because the relaxation effects are pretty immediate. The face mask, wand and red light hat makes the most sense for people who are willing to stick to a strict routine.

Keep in mind the science behind red light and PEMF therapy is still developing. Some studies are promising, but many are small, and results can vary from person to person. Still, after weeks of regular use, several of these tools earned a permanent spot in our routines. They’re well built, simple to use and easy to fit into an evening wind-down.

This year, I’m giving Lego lovers in my life sets that include the rechargeable Smart Bricks and Smart Tags, which debuted earlier this year. The Smart Tags communicate with the Smart Bricks, telling them to react with lights, colors and sounds depending on how your giftee interacts with them. Pokémon’s Training House with Pikachu Lego set comes with one Smart Brick, four Smart Tags and a charger, giving your giftee everything they need to experience the innovation. They’ll use the included 400 pieces to put together all the figures, and learn how to use the Smart Play System from the directions and a companion app.
Glasshouse Fragrances Kyoto in Bloom Candle and Spinning Carousel Set

Even if it feels like your recipient owns every type of candle, I can almost guarantee they haven’t seen anything like this set from Glasshouse Fragrances. It comes with the brand’s 13.4-ounce Kyoto in Bloom candle and a Spinning Carousel accessory, whose base sits on top of the jar so the festive charms hang above it. When your giftee lights the candle, the bright, flickering flame makes the dangling charms shimmer and twirl. They’ll also see the flame through the laser-cut windows on the sides of the festively decorated jar.
Catbird Confetti Custom Three Gold Charm Bracelet

I collect custom jewelry, and Catbird’s Confetti Charm Bracelet is one of my favorite pieces. Its dainty, minimalistic design is ideal for everyday wear, and I love that I have a connection to every detail. To personalize it for your giftee, you pick out the one, three, five or seven charms you think they’d find most meaningful on Catbird’s website. Then, jewelers in the brand’s Brooklyn studio add them to an adjustable chain and ship out the final handmade piece. You can choose from charms like letters, birthstones, zodiac signs and other symbols — each is priced individually.
We can help you find
Lennox Spice Village 6-Piece Garden District Spice Jar Set

Lennox recently released a second edition of its highly coveted Spice Village after retiring the original one in the early ‘90s — if your loved one has always dreamed of owning it, help them get started with this set of six jars. In future years, you can buy them additional sets to build up to the complete collection of 24 jars, and even expand into the brand’s other matching pieces. Each spice jar is shaped like a Victorian house, hand-painted with pastel colors and labeled with a spice’s name. The Garden District Spice Village Set comes with jars for rosemary, oregano, basil, allspice, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Jellycat Amusables Happy Boiled Egg

You can’t help but smile when you see a Jellycat, which is why it’s so easy to start collecting them. My favorite ones to give and receive are Amuseables, which are mini stuffies of animated objects like food and plants — there are even sports and weather themed ones. The Boiled Egg was my first Jellycat Amusable, and I’ve since gotten other iterations of it like a limited-edition Easter Bunny egg and a scientist. The stuffed toys are small, which makes them great desk or shelf decor, and they’re usually compact enough to fit inside a stocking.
Kodak Charmera Blind Box Digital Camera Keychain

While Kodak’s Charmera isn’t as fancy or rare as the vintage cameras many collectors have their eye on, it makes for a fun gift that aligns with something they’re passionate about. It also takes quality photos — our team was impressed when we tested it. The tiny, rechargeable digital camera comes on a keychain, takes photos and videos, and lets your giftee download content directly to their phone using the included USB-C cable. (They can also plug the camera or its SD card into a computer — the SD doesn’t come with the camera, so consider buying one for them.)
The Charmera lets your giftee choose from four frames and seven filters in photo mode, and they’ll be surprised by what their camera looks like when they open the package since it’s a blind box.
Ban.do Ceramic Oranges Salt and Pepper Shaker Set

My grandma has collected salt and pepper shakers for decades, which inspired me to do the same when I moved into my first apartment. My loved ones know that I’m always on the hunt for a quirky set, so they buy them for me during the holidays — perhaps you know someone who’d like them, too. Ban.do’s orange and orange juice carton shakers are exactly what I’d go for. Your giftee can display them on a shelf or make them part of their table’s centerpiece. And since they’re meant for dispensing seasonings, they’re functional in addition to being adorable.
Funko POP! Star Wars: The Mandalorian The Child

While some people are Funko POP! collectors, others have one of the brand’s figurines on their wishlist because it revolves around a specific franchise they’re a fan of, be it a TV show, movie, book series or sports team. That means there’s a Funko POP! out there for almost everyone. For example, if your giftee loves all things Star Wars, buy them a Funko POP! of their favorite character. I got my brother this one of The Mandalorian a few years ago, which he displays on his bookshelf at home.
The Life of a Showgirl: Sweat and Vanilla Perfume Portofino Orange Glitter Vinyl

Anyone who owns a record player will be grateful to unwrap a vinyl from one of their favorite bands or artists. Before I start shopping, I ask my friend or family member to give me a list of options they’re hoping to add to their library — that helps me avoid buying them something they already have. I always look for extra special versions of the vinyls they want, like this glittery orange version of Taylor Swift’s latest album, “The Life of a Showgirl.” There are also exclusive photos and album lyrics on the inside of the jacket.
Dcuk Spotty Hat and Boots Duckling

I’m a sucker for a tchotchke, so I naturally fell in love with Dcuk’s wooden statues the minute I saw them. I have five (and counting), and they’re the most asked about pieces of decor in my home — if a loved one notices them, I gift them their first one to start their collection. Each Dcuk stands in a different position, wears a unique outfit and has its own name on the tag. I display them together on a dedicated shelf, but your giftee can also scatter them around their living space and challenge guests to find them as they collect more.
Mackenzie-Childs Courtly Check Tea Kettle

Mackenzie-Childs’s black and white Courtly Check line is status symbol kitchen and homeware as far as I’m concerned. It includes pots and pans, countertop appliances, mugs, picture frames and holiday goods like ornaments and stockings — there’s something for you to gift your loved one well into the future if they’re as obsessed with the pattern as other Mackenzie-Child loyalists. The brand’s tea kettle is a solid piece to start their collection because it’s useful for boiling water, and it can stay on their stovetop, acting as a piece of decor.
Artifact Uprising Pressed Glass Photo Ornament

Adding a new ornament to my loved ones’ Christmas trees each year is one of my favorite traditions. In 2025, I personalized an ornament for each family through Artifact Uprising. The brand’s two-sided Pressed Glass Photo Ornament comes in oval, landscape and circle shapes, and you can upload any photo to be printed inside it — I chose to focus on pets in the past, but in 2026, I’m going with snapshots from our most memorable trips. You can also add a tag with the year to mark the keepsake. It comes with a ribbon that helps you hang it on branches.
Anthropologie Holiday in the City Stoneware Mug

Even though they probably have tons of them, getting a new mug will make the tea- or coffee-drinker in your life excited about sipping their favorite warm beverage. Anthropologie sells dozens of beautifully decorated options, like this one covered in a cityscape illustration. You can pick from scenes of Philadelphia, New York City, the North Pole, London, Paris, Toronto, Chicago and Dallas. The brand recommends hand-washing the mug and avoiding putting it in the microwave.
Jonathan Adler Vice Munchies Canister

Jonathan Adler’s Vice Munchies Canister has to be one of the chicest cookie jars I’ve ever seen — I’d bet your loved one who collects them would agree. Its 77-ounce capacity can house a batch of at least a dozen desserts, and the gasket around the lid creates an airtight seal to help them stay fresh. If the inside of the jar gets messy, they can put it in the dishwasher (top rack), but the brand recommends hand washing it.
Sonny Angel Mini Figure Fruit

Almost every NBC Selected staff member has Sonny Angels on their desk — a few of us started collecting them years ago, and now we buy them for each other on special occasions and trade figurines. Do the same with your giftee this holiday season. There are numerous varieties to choose from, like fruit, flowers, marine life, snacks and animals, but your recipient won’t know exactly which one is inside the blind box until they open it, which is half the fun.
Casio F91W Series Digital Watch

Have someone in your life who wants to start collecting watches? Casio makes digital ones that are an approachable entry point: they’re easy to use, durable for everyday wear and analog enough that they feel like a major departure from high-tech smartwatches. They’re also a more budget-friendly pick for gift givers. Casio’s F91W Series watch is water-resistant, and it can act as a stopwatch and alarm clock. It has about a seven year battery life, according to the brand.
Le Creuset Noel Mini Cocotte with Star Knob

Every year, Le Creuset debuts a few new pieces of cookware around the holidays, which the brand’s devotees wait for impatiently— your loved one might be one of them. This 24-ounce mini cocotte is a standout 2026 addition, especially due to details like a star-shaped knob and snowflake print on the lid. It’s made from stoneware and is covered in a non-porous, non-reactive and scratch-resistant glaze, so it doesn’t easily stain or absorb flavors. The interior is relatively nonstick, and it retains heat well.
Canelo & Co. Heirloom Pet Throw

I’ve  become obsessed with buying myself items that have my dog’s name and face on them — I swore I’d never be that mom, but I’m officially a year in and I have lots of chihuahua-dachshund knick knacks, in part thanks to gifts from my loved ones. If pet parents you know are anything like me (and NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans who also collects things emblazoned with her dog’s face), they’ll adore presents centered around their furry friends.

This blanket, for example, is completely customizable. You choose a color and size for the blanket, enter the pet’s name and upload a photo. Canelo emails you a proof of the illustration before weaving your recipient’s blanket to make sure it’s perfect.
“Something from Nothing” by Alison Roman

Expanding your recipient’s library is one of the most thoughtful things you can do for their book collection. I always put cookbooks on my wishlist, especially those published in the last year or so. Since I own all her other books, “Something from Nothing” by Alison Roman seemed like the appropriate option to ask Santa for next month. It’s filled with recipes that call for ingredients commonly found in people’s pantries, helping readers get food on the table quickly, deliciously and as mess-free as possible.
American Girl Girl of the Year 2027 Daisy Davenport

American Girl dolls are the first items I collected as a child — I know firsthand how special getting one is, so it should come from someone who understands their recipient’s connection to them now and what it will be in the future. Daisy Davenport is the 2027 Girl of the Year, making her one of the hottest gifts. Along with the doll, your giftee gets an illustrated book to help them better understand Daisy’s story.
Arsenal Home Jersey 26/27

“I’ve been a soccer fan for a while now, and I can honestly say that one of my absolute favorite parts of footy culture is the jerseys,” says NBC Selected associate reporter Ashley Morris, who collects them. Someone in your life may feel the same and appreciate getting a new jersey to represent their favorite team this holiday season.

“I have the jerseys of national teams from all over the world, but for me, nothing tops an Arsenal kit,” says Morris. “This jersey is a fan replica version, but it’s still lightweight and breathable, plus it has the gold Premier League championship patch on the sleeve. You can get it customized with your giftee’s favorite player, or even their own name, on the back.”

How I picked the best collectible gifts in 2026

To recommend the best collectible gifts, I drew on my own experience as an avid  collector and shopping editor who tests hundreds (if not thousands) of products year round. I also received recommendations from my team of shopping editors (and collectors) here at NBC Selected. Every option on my final list comes from a brand we’ve previously covered or that we’ve tried.
Some of the products were sent to us from brands as a courtesy for testing, and others we bought ourselves as gifts for loved ones, some are collectible gifts we received.
Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m a reporter at NBC Selected, where I’ve been writing gift guides for more than six years. I’ve covered topics like Advent calendars, gifts for coffee lovers and Hanukkah gifts. For this article, I compiled a list of the best collectible gifts of 2026, including highly-rated options, NBC Selected reader favorites and ones our team tested.

title: 33+ gifts for men that they’ll use well beyond the holiday season
summary: Whether you’re shopping for a brother, dad, grandfather, sibling or friend, there are a number of tech items, apparel and edible gifts that will make the men in your life happy.
story: Getting a unique and personal gift for the men in your life, whether it’s your husband, boyfriend, dad or brother, goes a long way in making their holiday memorable. Regardless if you’re shopping for a Christmas or Hanukkah gift, there are tons of unique items to choose from, all of which speak to different personalities, ages and hobbies.

To find the best gift ideas for men, including useful gadgets, entertainment, luxury pieces and items for foodies, I gathered a long list of products and got recommendations from my team of shopping experts at NBC Selected, who test hundreds (if not thousands) of products every year.

Best tech gifts for men
Apple AirPods 5 Wireless Earbuds

In addition to active noise cancellation, the AirPods 5 come with adaptive audio, which uses Transparency mode to automatically adjust noise settings based on your surroundings. Plus, it has spatial audio, which makes sounds and music more immersive. The AirPods 5 also have Live Translation, which translates conversations in different languages in real time. They get up to four hours of battery life with active noise cancellation and up to 20 hours in the case.
Hicober 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station

The Hicober tri-fold wireless charging station is the perfect accessory for your giftee to keep on their bedside table or on their desk at work. The three tiles of the charging station can charge their iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods at the same time. It collapses into the size of a coaster when not in use, so it’s easy to put in a suitcase, carry-on bag or gym duffel.
Amazon Ember Fire TV

The Amazon Fire TV is the perfect television set for a giftee who wants to improve their home entertainment system but also wants smart features that pair well with their other Amazon devices. With this TV, your giftee can use the Amazon Alexa-enabled remote to control its functions, including using voice commands to search for their favorite shows and movies. They can also use it to stream live TV without cable and watch tons of shows in 4K Ultra HD, according to Amazon. It comes with a stand, HDMI and ethernet outlets and Dolby Audio.
We can help you find
Apple AirTag (4-Pack)

I used to doubt whether I needed an Apple AirTag, until I almost lost my backpack a couple of years ago. Since then, having an AirTag gives me a major sense of relief when it comes to keeping track of my belongings. With this 2nd Generation AirTag, your giftee can track their wallet, keys, bags, suitcases, electronics and other personal items. They can easily pair the tags with their iPhone via Bluetooth. They can also keep track of their things via a map on their phone and program the trackers to sound an alert when they’re looking for an item.
Bose QuietComfort Headphones 2nd Generation

If your giftee prefers over-ear headphones over earbuds, consider surprising them with the newest version of the Bose QuietComfort Headphones. Aside from great sound quality, they have noise cancellation, padded ear cups and a battery that lasts up to one full day, according to the brand. The ear cups have buttons for volume control and the headphones have Awareness Mode, which allows them to listen to their favorite music or podcasts while staying aware of their surroundings. Plus, the headphones are now available in fun colors like Eucalyptus Green and Dewdrop Mint.
Amazon Echo Dot

The Amazon Echo Dot is a great gift idea for someone who wants to have a smart home but doesn’t know where to start. The Echo Dot is easy to set up and use, and with Amazon Alexa it can understand commands and questions. Your giftee can use it to check the weather, play music and control other smart home devices, such as a TV or a smart lamp.
Anker Power Bank

The Anker Power Bank is the most useful way for your giftee to keep their phone charged at all times, especially when they’re traveling or outdoors and don’t have access to a power outlet. What’s great about this power bank is that it connects to a phone in a way that lets you use the phone — calls and all — while it’s still charging. It also has a built-in lightning cable that folds downwards into itself, making it easy to store in a backpack or toiletry bag.
Nebula Capsule 3 Portable Projector

If you have a guy in mind that doesn’t have a TV at home or is short on space for a full home entertainment system, this mini projector is perfect for them. Around the size of a can of soda, the projector helps turn your giftee’s phone into their own personal television set.
Best food and home gifts for men
Chicken Shredder Twist Tool

I used to think that a shredder was obsolete, since you can technically shred chicken with forks or a stand mixer. However, this one completely changed my mind. I was immediately sold on this simple but practical gadget. If you’re shopping for a guy who cooks a lot of lean meat or poultry, they can use this to shred their food in seconds. You place the food onto the base, secure it with the lid, and then twist to shred — the more you twist, the more shredded the meat will be. It’s that simple to use.
Owala FreeSip 32-ounce Insulated Water Bottle

You probably see someone with an Owala water bottle at least once a day, and that’s because they are both durable and sleek. The FreeSip bottle has a combination spout and straw design, which gives your recipient the option to sip or swig their drink. It is also a great option for a guy who prefers a portable water bottle that can fit into a cup holder or the pocket of a backpack. I’ve had my Owala Tumbler for months, and it hasn’t gotten scratched or dented yet, and it’s great for carrying both still and carbonated water.
Fullstar Vegetable Chopper

I gave my parents this vegetable chopper for Christmas a few years ago and they’ve gotten a lot of use out of it ever since. It helps save a ton of time on tediously chopping vegetables, including onions — no one loves chopping onions. It has multiple attachments and blade types, meaning you can chop food in different sizes and even use it as a mandoline to make homemade potato chips and fries or thinly shaved zucchini for salads.
Ninja Slushi Frozen Drink Maker

The popular Ninja Slushi is a unique gift that’s perfect for the person in your life who loves experimenting with fun drinks. With the device, your giftee can make frozen margaritas, frosés, soda-based slushies and much more. All they have to do is pour their desired drink mix into the chilling cylinder on top and choose a setting to get started. NBC Selected video producer Josh Rios tested the Ninja Slushi in the office and made soda slushies for all of us in the summer.
Casamigos x Williams Sonoma Cocktail Gift Set

If your giftee is a fan of tequila, consider this gift set from Casamigos, which has everything they need to make their favorite drinks. It includes two cocktail mixers — one for making traditional margaritas and another for a blackberry basil smash — and two types of salt for rimming the glass: pink Himalayan and salty sweet orange. You can even make a gift basket with this and add a bottle of tequila and a couple of elegant glasses.
Instant Pot Electric Pressure Cooker

The Instant Pot electric pressure cooker was (and still is) a revolutionary cooking appliance, mainly because it eliminates the technicality and potential safety hazards of using a traditional pressure cooker. This appliance is ideal for a giftee who loves making foods that take hours to prepare and make tender (think beef stew, chili, pot roast, brisket) but doesn’t have the time to make them on a weeknight. It makes meals 70% faster than with a regular slow cooker, according to the brand. Plus, the easy-release steam lid makes it safe to open once food is done cooking.
Beast Mighty 850 Plus Personal Blender

I tested and wrote a review of the Beast blender when it first came out, and I loved how powerfully it blends different types of fruit and ingredients. This new version, the Mighty 850 Plus, is a middle-tier blender with 850-watts of power, so it’s definitely strong enough to blend things as hard as ice. I also appreciate how stylish it is, especially compared to similar blenders on the market. It comes with a large and small blending bottle, both of which you can just top with a lid to take with you. Plus, it’s made of durable BPA-free plastic, some parts of which are dishwasher safe.
Yeti French Press

While Yeti is known for having some of the best insulated water bottles, they also make other great kitchen appliances, such as this Yeti French Press, which I tested and reviewed. It’s easy to use with any type of coffee, it doesn’t stain easily or take a long time to clean, and I love how it keeps coffee hot a few hours after brewing. You can get it in 34 and 64 ounces in a couple different sizes in several colors and take it with you on outdoor adventures or outdoor sports games.
Cuisinart Stainless Steel Pan

This skillet was one of the first pans I had when I moved to New York City, and it lasted me years, even after I cooked just about everything in it. Whether it was a seared steak, burgers or chicken cutlets, meats cooked evenly in it and the pan didn’t get damaged in the process. Since it’s stainless steel, it’s ideal for a giftee who loves crispy or crunchy foods. It isn’t nonstick, so I suggest washing it by hand with mild soap and water.
Butcher Box Value Variety Box

I recommend gifting a Butcher Box subscription box to anyone who loves great quality meat, especially steak. I once received a box as a gift, and it was filled with copious amounts of steaks and ground beef that I used to make some of my favorite meals. I love that you can customize the box, based on what your giftee prefers.
Best fitness and wellness gifts for men
Hoka Ora Recovery Slide 3

NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman owns these slides because they’re comfortable and have arch support. They’re made from breathable EVA material and have a meta-rocker shape, meaning the front end curves upward which makes walking in them more comfortable, according to Hoka. They’re great for recovery after a run or workout, but your giftee can also just wear them around the house, too.
Hoka Clifton 11

We’ve tested walking shoes from Hoka, and NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin and I agree that Hoka’s Clifton collection has some of the most comfortable walking shoes we’ve ever tried. I wear mine all the time around my apartment or to run errands and my feet are never in pain, even after walking multiple miles. They’re incredibly soft on the soles of the feet, and they have medium cushioning. They have a high but flexible pull tab in the back and the brand’s popular meta-rocker shape on the front. The Clifton 11 is the newest version of the shoe, but many previous versions are also very comfortable and more likely to be on sale.
Theragun Therabody Mini Massage Gun

The Theragun Mini Massage Gun is a great gift idea for someone who regularly works out and wants to improve their recovery time. The massage gun helps relax muscles after strenuous exercise and relieves pain. It comes with three foam attachments to target different areas on the body and has three speed settings. Plus, it’s only around the size of a small dumbbell, so your giftee can take it with them to the gym.
Garmin Forerunner 165 Smartwatch

We’ve tested and written about several smartwatches and fitness trackers, and Garmin watches are always at the top of our list, including the Garmin Forerunner that we tested. It provides excellent data and has a great battery life (up to 11 days in smartwatch mode and up to 19 hours when it’s in GPS mode, according to the brand). It’s a perfect fitness tracker for athletes, particularly runners who want to hit a goal, according to Harry Rabinowitz, former NBC Selected tech reporter. It has a comfortable wristband, and tracks your sleep score, past recovery time and distance.
Oura Ring 5

We’ve tested every version of the Oura Ring and found that it’s a great option if your giftee finds ring fitness trackers to be more comfortable than a watch or bracelet. It can help track heart health, sleep, metabolic health and more. The Oura Ring 5 is the newest version and compared to older versions it’s lighter and thinner.
Best apparel and accessories gifts for men
Jisulife Portable Neck Fan

If your giftee lives in a particularly warm climate or if they’re chronically hot, this portable neck fan is the most thoughtful gift. On a full charge, it has up to 16 hours of runtime, so it’s perfect for rounds of golf or when he’s walking around a crowded theme park for hours. The fan resembles a pair of over-ear headphones and is only 9.5 ounces. Plus, it’s adjustable, so it can fit around different size necks.
Steady State SuperLoft Crew Sweatshirt

While I usually get accessories like small crossbody bags from Lululemon, I always tell people about its crewneck sweatshirts, which are incredibly soft and hold up well after many washes. This version, the Steady State SuperLoft Crew, has a modern, relaxed crop hem, which means it doesn’t bunch up. I also love that it comes in a few different muted colors and has a soft fleece feel on the inside.
Carhartt Classic Laptop Backpack

This backpack from Carhartt is ideal for a giftee who’s looking for a sturdy backpack that’s also spacious. It’s made of water-repellent material, a large main compartment and a pocket that can fit a 15-inch laptop. It also has two side pockets, which your giftee can use to hold a reusable water bottle or other small belongings, such as earbuds.
Adidas Gazelle Indoor Shoes

If you want to give your giftee a trendy shoe, the Gazelles are the perfect choice. These casual sneakers have a similar look to the popular Adidas Sambas, but their platforms and uppers are a different material and style. The Gazelles are great shoes for everyday activities, with rubber outsoles and suede and mesh uppers. Plus, they’re available in a range of designs, so you can choose the one that best suits your giftee.
Abercrombie & Fitch Essential Cinched Sweatpants

These sweatpants have an elastic waistband and cuffs at the bottom, making them both comfortable to wear and easy to adjust. They have an ideal loose fit and they’re perfect for wearing to bed or to run errands. Plus, they have pockets that are large enough to actually hold stuff you need, as well as one pocket on the back. You can get them in short, regular and long lengths.
REI Gift Card

As a commerce editor, I regularly cover sales at REI, which is a mainstay for outdoor and fitness items. If your giftee enjoys running, camping, cycling or other outdoor activities, they’ll surely get a lot of use out of this gift card. The brand sells practically everything an outdoorsy person could need, including fitness trackers, tents, sleeping pads, comfortable socks and boots for trails and rough terrain.
Buck Mason Field-Spec Cotton T-Shirt

This simple but durable white t-shirt from Buck Mason is made from durable material and has a heavy feel. A bestseller for the brand, the shirt is made from 310 GSM (grams per square meter) jersey cotton and has a classic fit that isn’t too tight or oversized, according to the brand. Your giftee can wear it as is, or with a button-down shirt over it for a more dressed-up look when going out.
Steve Madden Natan Penny Loafers

A good pair of loafers is a staple for any guy, especially since it’s a shoe that can easily pivot between casual and formal. These loafers from Steve Madden have become one of my favorites, since they have a traditional silhouette, but they include a unique white stitching that runs along the upper part of the shoe, which I always get compliments on. They come in three different versions, though I love the monochromatic one since it goes with so many outfits.
Carhartt Oil Tan Leather Trifold Wallet

I upgraded my wallet to this durable one from Carhartt (bifold style), and I love the look and feel of it — it’s smooth on the outside and it doesn’t get scratched easily. It has a clear panel for my ID, which is both secure and easy to remove when I’m at the airport. It also has plenty of space for my cards and cash.
Best travel gifts for men
Ostrichpillow Go Travel Pillow

We previously tested the Ostrich Pillow, which won an NBC Selected Travel Award for best travel pillow a couple of years ago, and it continues to be a go-to for our team. If you’re looking for a gift for a man who travels a lot but often has trouble getting sleep on a plane, this pillow is the answer. It provides great support and he can also use it as an eye mask.
Le Labo Santal 33 Travel Tube Refill Set

I’ve always been an advocate for anything from Le Labo, particularly the scent Santal 33, which is easily one of the best eau de parfums for men. While there are a lot of colognes that get a lot of hype, this one is actually worth it. This small travel tube set is the perfect way to test out the sandalwood scent without fully committing to it. Plus, it’s easy to stow in a carry-on or suitcase when traveling.
Patagonia Black Hole Duffel

The Patagonia Black Hole duffel bag won an NBC Selected Travel Award, thanks to its spaciousness and durability. The bag functions as both a duffel bag you’d carry in hand, as well as a backpack, since it has two straps on the top you can wear on your shoulders. It’s the perfect size for flights and short trips or even for use as a gym bag.
Away The Carry-On

I got this popular suitcase from Away as a Christmas gift a few years ago, and I love how spacious it is, while also being the perfect size for a carry-on. It has a minimalist look and a locking zipper that’s TSA-compliant. The wheels are incredibly smooth on different surfaces, so I can move it around with either two wheels, or let it stand up and roll it with four. Plus, it fits several of the brand’s multiple packing cubes, which you can get in corresponding colors to match your luggage.

title: Cornell faculty senate votes no confidence in administration’s handling of sexual assault
summary: Members of the Cornell University faculty senate on Friday issued a vote of no confidence in the administration’s ability to manage the response to an alleged sexual assault at a fraternity house in 2024, according to the university.
story: Members of the Cornell University faculty senate on Friday issued a vote of no confidence in the administration’s ability to manage the response to an alleged sexual assault at a fraternity house in 2024, according to the university.

The governing body took up the issue after a former student, known as Jane Doe, alleged she was sexually assaulted and forced to take drugs at the Chi Phi fraternity house from Oct. 19 to 20, 2024. The allegations, detailed in a lawsuit the woman filed in September, led to widespread criticism of the university and calls for reform from students and alumni.
The senate’s resolution states that the body “has no confidence in the ability of the central administration to effectively address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault at Cornell University.”

It does not recommend removals or suggest how to manage the controversy’s fallout. It passed by a vote of 75-50, with five abstentions and five members not voting, according to a copy of the results obtained by NBC News.

The vote will not directly affect leadership decisions at the institution, including whether President Michael Kotlikoff remains in his role. The board of trustees, which has the authority to replace him, can consider the finding in its decisions but suggested in a statement Friday that no immediate changes were expected.

“The Board of Trustees remains confident that President Kotlikoff and his administration are the right leaders to thoughtfully and comprehensively address the serious problem of sexual assault on our campus,” chair Anne Meinig Smalling said.
Smalling highlighted recent changes implemented by leadership.

“They have already taken several important steps to this end, including adding staff to the Cornell Office of Civil Rights, expanding in-person sexual assault prevention education, and hiring more victim advocates,” Smalling said. “The administration will continue to build on that progress with more initiatives to be launched in the weeks and months ahead.”
Faculty senators who sponsored the resolution called the decision “a reckoning” for the university.

“It is a call for real, systemic change; not a slow-moving taskforce, weakly enforced ban on fraternity parties, or expensive [public relations] damage control, but meaningful, evidence-based steps to reduce the incidence of sexual assault on campus and provide significant support to and justice for survivors,” the sponsors wrote in a statement.
Jane Doe and her attorney have alleged that Cornell failed to support her through the reporting process and subsequent investigation.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“We are hopeful that this will be yet another step forward to educate and support the Cornell community by addressing the longstanding scourge of sexual assault on campus,” said Jane Doe’s attorney Thomas Giuffra.
Jane Doe accused seven members of the fraternity of participating in a sexual assault, which she told police began with a consensual threesome but resulted in unwanted sex and ketamine consumption.
All seven men accused in the incident deny the allegations. Two were expelled from the university after an internal civil rights proceeding, and others faced less severe punishments from the school.
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said he declined to pursue a criminal case in November 2024 based on a six-page statement from Jane Doe.

New York Attorney General Letitia James was appointed by Gov. Kathy Hochul last month to investigate the matter and consider whether criminal charges are supported. Two of the defendants initiated court proceedings aimed at disqualifying James based on what they argue are biased statements of support for Jane Doe that James posted on social media.

On Thursday, several defendants joined an Article 78 proceeding in Sullivan County that was recently filed by lawyers for one of the fraternity brothers, Gillio Lopes. Diego Sarabia, Scott Kretzschmar, Scott Norris and Winston Lee, who are co-defendants in Jane Doe’s lawsuit, were added to the petition in support of Lopes’ request.
Two remaining defendants, Matthew Ingalls and Jonathan Newell, do not have representation in the civil case and did not respond to Lopes’ attorneys.

On Wednesday, James announced her appointment of a former federal prosecutor to direct the investigation. That attorney, Jacqueline Kelly, will lead a team under James to conduct an independent inquiry into the sexual assault allegations.

Lopes’ lawyers argued in court papers that unless James recuses herself, the appointment does not change their position on the existence of a conflict. James has said her office is fully capable of conducting a fact-based, unbiased review.
James has also said her comments were merely an expression of empathy for Jane Doe.

Lee’s attorney previously filed a separate motion in Tompkins County Supreme Court seeking to block James from any grand jury proceeding, arguing that she had exhibited bias. A decision is expected Nov. 13.

At a virtual news conference after the faculty senate vote Friday, the proposal’s lead sponsor, Paul Ortiz, said the idea came “after hearing from scores of current students, alumni, staff and faculty that the Jane Doe case was the tip of the iceberg.”
